Pancho]] |blank1_name = Political party |blank1_info = {{Color box|{{party color|National Unity Party (Philippines)}}|border=darkgray}} [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|NUP]] |blank2_name = Congressional bloc |blank2_info = Majority }} '''Bulacan's 2nd congressional district''' is one of the seven [[congressional districts of the Philippines]] in the province of [[Bulacan]]. It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 1916 and earlier in the [[Philippine Assembly]] from 1907 to 1916.{{cite web |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=April 19, 2020 |archive-date=March 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316064243/http://congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |url-status=dead }} The district consists of the city of [[Baliwag]] and the municipalities of [[Bustos, Bulacan|Bustos]] and [[Plaridel, Bulacan|Plaridel]]. It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Tina Pancho]] of the [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|National Unity Party]] (NUP).{{cite web|url=https://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=January 23, 2023}} Prior to its second dissolution in 1972, the second district encompassed the eastern Bulacan municipalities of [[Angat, Bulacan|Angat]], Baliuag (Baliwag), [[Bocaue]], [[Marilao]], [[Meycauayan]], [[Norzagaray]], [[Obando, Bulacan|Obando]], [[San Ildefonso, Bulacan|San Ildefonso]], [[San Jose del Monte]], [[San Miguel, Bulacan|San Miguel]], [[San Rafael, Bulacan|San Rafael]], [[Santa Maria, Bulacan|Santa Maria]], and [[Valenzuela, Metro Manila|Valenzuela]] (formerly Polo). It also included the municipality of Polo, which last consisted of the northern portion of the present-day Valenzuela,{{cite PH act|chamber=EO|number=401, s. 1960|date=July 21, 1960|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1960/07/21/executive-order-no-401-s-1960/|title=Creating the municipality of Valenzuela in the province of Bulacan|accessdate=April 24, 2022 |publisher=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)|Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines]] }} until it was merged with Valenzuela in 1963.{{cite PH act|chamber=EO|number=46, s. 1963|date=September 11, 1963| url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1963/09/11/executive-order-no-46-s-1963/|title=Consolidating and Reuniting the Territories of the Municipalities of Polo and Valenzuela Into a Municipality to Be Known as Valenzuela|accessdate=November 18, 2023 |publisher=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)|Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines]] }} Following the restoration of the [[Congress of the Philippines|Congress]] in 1987, the district was reconfigured to encompass [[Balagtas, Bulacan|Balagtas]], Baliwag, Bocaue, Bustos, [[Guiguinto]], [[Pandi, Bulacan|Pandi]], and Plaridel, amid the addition of two districts for Bulacan.{{cite web|title=The 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines| url=https://www.chanrobles.com/ordinance.htm| publisher=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=April 10, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|title=THE 1987 CONSTITUTION OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES – ORDINANCE|website=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)|Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines]]|accessdate=August 18, 2023}} Balagtas, Bocaue, Guiguinto, and Pandi were later excised from the district to form the [[Bulacan's 5th congressional district|fifth district]] effective 2022, leaving it with three in its current jurisdiction.{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=11546|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2021/05/26/republic-act-no-11546/|publisher=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)|Official Gazette of the Republic
